costa-rica.overview: Costa Rica has warm water and consistent waves for all levels up and down its Pacific coast. Beginners learn on Tamarindo's gentle beach breaks and intermediates head to Santa Teresa. Experts go south to Pavones for a long left-hand point break, or to Playa Hermosa near Jacó for heavy beach break barrels. The Pacific is best from May to November on south swells, though September and October are the wettest months. The Caribbean side has a smaller scene, mainly Salsa Brava near Puerto Viejo in winter.

months.1: Dry season brings smaller northwest swells and clean 3-5 ft waves with offshore mornings along the Pacific coast. Tamarindo is perfect for beginners and Santa Teresa has fun intermediate peaks. On the Caribbean side, Salsa Brava can work on winter swells. 82 F, no wetsuit needed.
months.2: Smaller northwest swells keep the Pacific coast clean at 3-5 ft, with offshore winds in the mornings. Tamarindo suits beginners and Santa Teresa has fun intermediate peaks. 82 F, no wetsuit needed.
months.3: Northwest swells continue as the first south swells arrive, lifting waves to 4-6 ft. Santa Teresa has consistent intermediate waves and skies stay sunny before the rains.
months.4: The transition month brings more frequent south swells to the Pacific coast. Playa Hermosa near Jacó sees heavier 5-7 ft waves for experts, while beginners can still find sheltered spots near Tamarindo.
months.5: The rains begin and south swells build to consistent 5-7 ft on the Pacific coast, with clean mornings and showers later in the day. Experts surf the heavy, hollow beach break at Playa Hermosa near Jacó, and beginners stay on Tamarindo's sheltered inside sections.
months.6: Prime south swell season delivers consistent 5-8 ft waves, with offshore mornings and afternoon showers. Experts ride the long left-hand point break at Pavones and the hollow beach break at Playa Hermosa near Jacó, while beginners stay on Tamarindo's sheltered inside sections.
months.7: The biggest, most consistent south swells of the year hit the Pacific coast at 5-8 ft, with morning offshores and showers most afternoons. Pavones peels for experts, Playa Hermosa near Jacó is at its heaviest, and Tamarindo's inside sections suit beginners.
months.8: South swells stay strong at 5-8 ft, and mornings are the best window before the afternoon showers and onshore breeze. Pavones and Playa Hermosa near Jacó stay good for experts, and Santa Teresa suits intermediates.
months.9: Swells are still strong at 5-7 ft, but September is among the wettest months on the Pacific coast, so expect rain and sloppier wind after the morning offshores. Pavones and Playa Hermosa near Jacó still deliver for experts.
months.10: Among the wettest months on the Pacific side: south swells keep rolling at 4-6 ft, but heavy rain and muddy roads make surf trips harder. Surf early, before the afternoon downpours.
months.11: South swells become less frequent, dropping average wave heights to 4-6 ft, and the rains begin to ease. The heavy shorebreak at Playa Hermosa near Jacó remains fun for experts, while intermediates find excellent conditions at Santa Teresa.
months.12: The Pacific coast shifts back to northwest swells with clean 3-5 ft waves as the dry season begins. Tamarindo is ideal for beginners learning to stand up on gentle peaks.

ghana.overview: Busua Beach offers gentle, sandy beach breaks that are ideal for beginners learning to surf. Waves are usually 2-4 ft, with the biggest and most consistent south swells from about June to September, so it is a reliable but modest destination. Experienced surfers will find small, quiet peaks, but should watch for strong rips and a rocky bottom at the outer point.

months.1: Small, gentle 2-3 ft beach breaks roll in at Busua, quiet and beginner-friendly, with 78 F water and no wetsuit needed.

months.4: South swells begin to build, lifting Busua's beach breaks to a gentle 2-4 ft that suits beginners. 78 F water, no wetsuit needed.
months.5: South swells keep building, bringing steadier 2-4 ft peaks to Busua. The main rainy season brings showers, but the waves keep rolling.
months.6: The strongest, most consistent south swells of the year start to arrive at Busua, giving reliable 3-4 ft waves for beginners and improvers. Showers are likely, and the rips can be strong.
months.7: Peak south swell season brings the most consistent 3-4 ft waves of the year to Busua's beach breaks, still gentle enough for beginners. Watch for strong rips and the rocky bottom at the outer point.
months.8: Peak south swell season brings the most consistent 3-4 ft waves of the year to Busua's beach breaks, still gentle enough for beginners. Watch for strong rips and the rocky bottom at the outer point.

months.10: Swells ease to 2-4 ft during a second, lighter rainy period. The beach breaks stay gentle for beginners, and rips can be strong.
months.11: Smaller 2-3 ft south swells return to Busua's gentle beach breaks, with beginner-friendly peaks and strong rips to watch for.
